historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (41.0%) diverges sharply from net revenue 3yr CAGR (29.7%) because equity is inflated by retained earnings compounding off a small FY2022 base and by FX translation gains booked to OCI (e.g. +$67.7m FY2026), not because the underlying business is compounding book value at 41%/yr -- per the ticker-specific mandate, net revenue CAGR (not equity CAGR) is used as the primary growth driver precisely because of this distortion (here from retained-earnings/FX effects rather than buybacks, which is the more common Wise distortion). EPS 3yr CAGR (54.9%) also diverges from revenue growth, reflecting operating leverage off a near-breakeven FY2022 base -- not used as primary driver. Reported FCF CAGR (35.9%) is NOT reliable either: it is inflated by FY2025's outsized 31.8% owner-FCF margin (a working-capital/tax-timing high-water mark) and depressed by FY2026's deliberate heavy-investment year (19.1% owner-FCF margin) -- the owner-FCF series swings between 12.8% (FY2022) and 31.8% (FY2025) margin on net revenue with no clean trend, which is exactly why Step 1c mandates a component build (EBITDA-SBC-D&A-tax-capex-WC) rather than extrapolating any single historical FCF growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: SBC-adjusted (owner) FCF 3yr CAGR (38.3%) is actually ABOVE the reported FCF 3yr CAGR (35.9%) for Wise, the opposite of the usual SBC-dilution pattern -- this is because Wise's SBC is a small (~3.8-7.6%) and DECLINING share of net revenue (nil-cost/near-nil-strike option plan, not a Silicon-Valley-style RSU program), and FY2026's step-up in SBC ($95.5m from $74.6m) coincided with a reported-FCF dip, so the SBC deduction understates FY2026 relative to FY2025 by a similar proportion as reported FCF understates it. This is a genuinely different SBC profile than DUOL/US tech peers: Wise's buybacks ($473.4m FY2026) already run ~5x SBC ($95.5m), so uncovered dilution is zero and the share-count mechanism (not the FCF-deduction mechanism) is where SBC would normally bite -- it doesn't, because Wise over-covers it via buybacks.

valuation_philosophy: Wise is modeled as a decelerating high-growth fintech using a 10-year component-built owner-FCF model, not a flat-margin extrapolation of the FY2026 heavy-investment year. Net revenue CAGR (29.7% trailing 3yr) is the growth driver, not equity CAGR (41.0%, inflated by retained-earnings/FX-translation compounding) or reported FCF (which swings 12.8%-31.8% margin on net revenue with no clean trend due to working-capital/tax timing). Owner FCF is built bottom-up each year: adjusted EBITDA margin ramps from the FY2026 trough (28.5%, post the deliberate compliance/tech/marketing reinvestment step-up) toward a mature 36% (base case) -- materially below the pre-reset FY2024/25 peak of ~42.5%/38.7%, honoring the mandate that Servicing+G&A opex near 30-31% of net revenue is now a permanent structural floor, not a temporary spike. SBC is deducted at its actual (small, ~3.8% of revenue, declining) level -- Wise's near-nil-strike option program plus a buyback ($473.4m FY2026) running ~5x SBC means uncovered dilution is zero and the share count stays flat, the opposite dynamic to DUOL. Working capital is modeled as a net DRAG scaling with revenue growth (not a subscription-style deferred-revenue tailwind), matching Wise's actual multi-year pattern. Net corporate cash (+$1,873.7m, replacing a near-zero net-debt assumption in the prior model) is added to enterprise value, with the offsetting corporate interest income ($63.0m) stripped from FCF to avoid double-counting. WACC (11.5% base) explicitly stacks a 200bp regulatory risk premium across the OCC charter denial, the Belgian criminal AML investigation into Wise Europe SA, and the pattern of repeat AML findings across three jurisdictions in twelve months, plus a 25bp governance premium for the CEO's extended supervoting control -- on top of a ~9.0% base cost of capital for a large, profitable, net-cash global payments platform. The historical-multiple sanity check passes without requiring any fix: base-case implied multiples sit below Wise's own FY2024-26 trading range and assume no multiple expansion (implied exit multiples of 9.3-14.8x vs today's trailing 21.1x EV/owner-FCF). || UPDATED 2026-08-28: the terminal adj-EBITDA margin was cut from 36% to 30% and flattened from Y7 after comparison against two independently built external workbooks, both of which put the mature margin materially lower (27.5% and 30.0%). Combined with a +11.6% USD price move, WISE goes from ~13% base-case upside to ~12% OVERVALUED, and the probability-weighted case from +16.6% to -8.5%. The honest read is that the prior model's headline upside rested on a terminal margin above the company's own pre-investment peak. || 2026-09-22 revision: base margins constrained to management's guided band (terminal EBIT ~22.4% ex corporate interest), one 9.5% USD discount rate for all scenarios with the regulatory risk carried in the bear flows and house 15/50/35 weights (no triple charge), working capital at the three-year actual drag, and shares and cash on the same balance-sheet date. Base moves 876p -> ~920p; the scenario spread narrows and entry prices fall ~100p.

unchanged_and_why.net_cash_base_bull: -$1,873.7m. An earlier read suspected the EMTN bond was not netted; it is - CoreFloat_Inputs.md deducts the GBP250m 5.10% 2030 carrying value (-328.7) and accrued interest (-6.0) from corporate liquid assets 2,208.4 to reach 1,873.7. unchanged_and_why.shares_outstanding: 1,002.5m point-in-time fully diluted, Class B excluded. Both externals use backward-looking weighted averages (1,029.7m / 1,019m).
unchanged_and_why.da_and_capex: 0.58% / 1.0% of revenue, matching FY2026 actuals (0.58% / 0.86%). The 28-Aug workbook's 2.8% / 4.0% are its own documented estimation error.

scenario_narratives.base: NBB order met by 31-Jan-27; a Belgian summons resolves as a fine in the tens of millions plus a year of headlines. FY27 net revenue ~17% (guide: middle of 15-20%), fading ~1.5pt/yr to 5.5%. EBITDA margin 28.5% fading to 26% as the interest payout is enabled and rates normalise; terminal EBIT at the top of the ex-interest guided band. SBC 3.7% to 3.0%, settled through the Employee Share Trust. Working capital drags at the three-year average.
scenario_narratives.bull: Regulatory items close for immaterial sums; Wise Platform reaches its 10%-of-volume target, a US charter lands under GENIUS by FY28, balances grow faster than rates fall and the interest payout never structurally arrives, so the reported 20-25% IBT band persists (EBITDA ~30%). Net revenue ~21% fading to 7%.
scenario_narratives.bear: NBB deadline missed or met with conditions; EEA onboarding restricted for two years, criminal fine plus multi-year remediation, compliance cost permanently higher and the customer-interest payout arrives. Growth 4% for two years, 23% terminal EBITDA, SBC stuck at 3.8%. The ~$600m cash cost is documented but not modelled (single bridge).
